unit_label: Module A: correspondent banking, NRI loans and LRS conditions - additional assessment

facts.statement: A correspondent bank is a financial institution in a host country that provides services to banks present elsewhere; the bank in the home country that relies on it as its agent is the respondent bank. Banks use correspondents to reach foreign markets and clients without opening branches abroad, avoiding the cost of a branch network and branch licensing restrictions.

Account services of a correspondent bank require an account relationship with the foreign bank: clearing house functions (outward and inward payments, collections, statements, reimbursement of LC claims), collections of bills and cheques, payments, overdrafts and loan facilities, and investment of overnight surplus balances.
facts.locator: Printed p. 64, section 3.2.2 A, items (i) to (v)

facts.statement: Other correspondent services do not normally require an account relationship and rest on the relationship and credit assessment: letter of credit advising and confirmation, buyer's and supplier's credit, bankers acceptances, guarantees, foreign exchange services, custodial services, trade referrals and credit reports, fund raising services and training.

Loans in India against NRE or FCNR(B) deposits may be given to the account holder or to third parties, subject to usual margin requirements, but may not be used for relending, agricultural or plantation activities, or investment in real estate. For a third-party loan there must be no direct or indirect foreign exchange consideration for the depositor pledging the deposit. A loan to the account holder may be repaid by adjusting the deposit, by inward remittance or from the holder's NRO balances. Premature withdrawal of a deposit is not available while a loan against it is outstanding. Loans outside India against NRE or FCNR(B) deposits are allowed through branches or correspondents of the bank, subject to margin; they are not permitted against NRO balances.
facts.locator: Q3, rows "Loans in India" and "Loans outside India"; S03 printed pp. 82-83 agrees

facts.statement: An authorised dealer or a housing finance institution approved by the National Housing Bank may give an NRI or PIO a rupee housing loan to acquire residential accommodation in India. The amount, margin and repayment period are the same as for a resident; the loan may not be credited to an NRE, FCNR(B) or NRNR account; it must be fully secured by an equitable mortgage of the property, with a lien on other assets in India if necessary; instalments, interest and charges may be paid by remittance from abroad, from funds in an NRE, FCNR(B), NRNR, NRO or NRSR account, from rental income from the property, or by a relative in India through an account-to-account transfer; the interest rate must conform to RBI and NHB directives.
facts.locator: Section 4; S03 printed p. 83 agrees on the main conditions but omits the relative's transfer

facts.statement: The authorised dealer must ensure that payment is received out of the remitter's own funds by a cheque drawn on the applicant's account, by debit to the account, or by demand draft or pay order (or card of the cardholder); must certify that the remittance is not made directly or indirectly by or to ineligible entities; must keep on record the information on which the transaction was done; must refuse in writing and, if it suspects contravention, report to the Reserve Bank where the applicant refuses to comply; must follow KYC and anti-money laundering rules; and, for a new customer making a capital account remittance, must carry out due diligence and obtain the previous year's bank statement or the latest tax assessment order or return.

Remittances under the scheme are reported in FETERS in the normal course, and authorised dealer banks are guided by FED Master Direction No. 18/2015-16 on Reporting under FEMA, 1999. Banks, including those with no presence in India, must obtain prior RBI approval for schemes they market in India to residents for soliciting foreign currency deposits for overseas branches or acting as agents for overseas mutual funds or other foreign financial services companies.

payload.stem_md: In correspondent banking, what is the bank in the home country that relies on a bank abroad as its agent called?

options.text_md: The correspondent bank
options.explanation_md: The correspondent bank is the agent abroad, not the home bank.

options.text_md: The respondent bank
options.explanation_md: The bank at home that relies on a bank abroad as its agent is the respondent bank.

options.text_md: The clearing bank
options.explanation_md: A clearing bank handles settlement and is not the relying bank.

options.text_md: The nostro bank
options.explanation_md: A nostro bank is the one holding the account abroad.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The bank at home that relies on a bank abroad as its agent is the respondent bank.

payload.stem_md: Why does a bank use correspondent banks rather than open its own branches abroad?

options.text_md: Because correspondent banks may not charge fees
options.explanation_md: Correspondent banks do charge fees.

options.text_md: Because branches abroad are forbidden to all Indian banks
options.explanation_md: Branches abroad are not forbidden to all Indian banks.

options.text_md: To reach foreign markets and clients without the cost of a branch network and branch licensing restrictions
options.explanation_md: Correspondent banks let a bank reach foreign markets without a branch network and branch licensing limits.

options.text_md: Because it avoids all exchange control rules
options.explanation_md: Exchange control rules still apply.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Correspondent banks let a bank reach foreign markets without a branch network and branch licensing limits.

payload.stem_md: Which correspondent service needs an account relationship between the two banks?

options.text_md: Advising a letter of credit
options.explanation_md: This rests on relationship and credit assessment.

options.text_md: Issuing a credit report on a buyer
options.explanation_md: No account is needed.

options.text_md: Training of staff
options.explanation_md: No account is needed.

options.text_md: Payments and collections handled through the clearing house function on the foreign bank
options.explanation_md: Clearing, payments, collections, overdraft and investment of overnight balances need an account.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Clearing house functions, collections, payments, overdrafts and loan facilities and investment of overnight balances require an account relationship.

payload.stem_md: Which of the following correspondent bank services does NOT normally need an account with the correspondent?

options.text_md: Confirmation of a letter of credit
options.explanation_md: Confirming a letter of credit is a service the correspondent gives without needing an account.

options.text_md: Payment of an outward remittance from the respondent's account
options.explanation_md: Paying an outward remittance from the respondent's account needs an account.

options.text_md: Statement and reimbursement of LC claims through the account
options.explanation_md: Statements and LC reimbursements through the account need an account.

options.text_md: Investment of the respondent's overnight surplus
options.explanation_md: Investing overnight surplus needs an account.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Confirming a letter of credit is a service the correspondent gives without needing an account.

payload.stem_md: An NRI wants a loan in India against his NRE fixed deposit and then asks to withdraw the deposit prematurely while the loan is outstanding. What is the position?

options.text_md: He may withdraw at once and repay later
options.explanation_md: Withdrawing at once and repaying later would remove the security.

options.text_md: He may withdraw if the bank agrees
options.explanation_md: The bank's agreement cannot override the rule.

options.text_md: Premature withdrawal is not available while the loan is outstanding
options.explanation_md: Premature withdrawal of an NRE deposit is not available while the loan against it is outstanding.

options.text_md: He may withdraw half the deposit
options.explanation_md: Withdrawing half is not permitted either.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Premature withdrawal of an NRE deposit is not available while the loan against it is outstanding.

payload.stem_md: For what purpose may a loan in India against an NRE deposit NOT be used?

options.text_md: Personal expenses
options.explanation_md: Not barred by this rule.

options.text_md: Investment in real estate
options.explanation_md: Relending, agriculture, plantation and real estate investment are barred.

options.text_md: Meeting business working capital in a permitted activity
options.explanation_md: Not barred by this rule.

options.text_md: Purchase of a car
options.explanation_md: Not barred by this rule.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Loans against NRE or FCNR(B) deposits may not be used for relending, agricultural or plantation activities or real estate investment.

payload.stem_md: A loan outside India is sought against which balance?

options.text_md: An NRO balance
options.explanation_md: An NRO balance is not eligible for this loan.

options.text_md: Any resident rupee deposit
options.explanation_md: A resident rupee deposit is not the permitted security.

options.text_md: A foreign currency deposit of a resident
options.explanation_md: A resident's foreign currency deposit is not the permitted security.

options.text_md: An NRE or FCNR(B) deposit through a branch or correspondent of the bank, subject to margin; not an NRO balance
options.explanation_md: A loan outside India may be granted against an NRE or FCNR(B) deposit, subject to margin, and not against an NRO balance.

payload.correct_explanation_md: A loan outside India may be granted against an NRE or FCNR(B) deposit, subject to margin, and not against an NRO balance.

payload.stem_md: Into which account may the proceeds of a rupee housing loan to an NRI NOT be credited?

options.text_md: An NRE, FCNR(B) or NRNR account
options.explanation_md: Proceeds of a rupee housing loan to an NRI may not be credited to an NRE, FCNR(B) or NRNR account.

options.text_md: An NRO account
options.explanation_md: An NRO account is permitted.

options.text_md: The seller's account
options.explanation_md: The seller's account may receive the payment.

options.text_md: A joint account with a resident relative
options.explanation_md: A joint account with a resident relative can be used.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Proceeds of a rupee housing loan to an NRI may not be credited to an NRE, FCNR(B) or NRNR account.

payload.stem_md: From which source may the instalments of an NRI's housing loan be paid?

options.text_md: Only by remittance from abroad
options.explanation_md: Other sources are allowed.

options.text_md: Only from rental income
options.explanation_md: Other sources are allowed.

options.text_md: Remittance from abroad, funds in NRE, FCNR(B), NRNR, NRO or NRSR accounts, rental income from the property, or a relative in India by account transfer
options.explanation_md: All of these are allowed.

options.text_md: Only from the NRE account
options.explanation_md: Other sources are allowed.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Instalments may be paid by remittance from abroad, from the listed accounts, from rental income, or by a relative in India through an account-to-account transfer.

payload.stem_md: An authorised dealer receives a remittance request under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme. How must payment be received?

options.text_md: In cash from any person
options.explanation_md: Cash from any person is not allowed.

options.text_md: Out of the remitter's own funds by cheque on his account, debit to his account, demand draft or pay order (or his own card)
options.explanation_md: Under the LRS, payment is received from the remitter's own funds by cheque, debit, draft or pay order, or his own card.

options.text_md: By cheque drawn by a friend
options.explanation_md: A cheque from a friend is a third party payment.

options.text_md: From a loan from an overseas lender
options.explanation_md: A loan from an overseas lender is not the remitter's own funds.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Under the LRS, payment is received from the remitter's own funds by cheque, debit, draft or pay order, or his own card.

payload.stem_md: A new customer asks for a capital account remittance under the scheme. What additional step must the bank take?

options.text_md: Obtain approval of the Reserve Bank in every case
options.explanation_md: Reserve Bank approval is not needed in every case.

options.text_md: Take a cash margin of ten per cent
options.explanation_md: A ten per cent cash margin is not required.

options.text_md: Nothing beyond KYC
options.explanation_md: More than KYC is required.

options.text_md: Carry out due diligence and obtain the previous year's bank statement or the latest tax assessment order or return
options.explanation_md: For a new customer's capital account remittance the bank does due diligence and obtains the last year's bank statement or latest tax assessment or return.

payload.correct_explanation_md: For a new customer's capital account remittance the bank does due diligence and obtains the last year's bank statement or latest tax assessment or return.

payload.stem_md: Through which system are LRS remittances reported?

options.text_md: FETERS, in the normal course
options.explanation_md: LRS remittances are reported through FETERS in the normal course.

options.text_md: The bank's internal register only
options.explanation_md: The bank's own register alone is not enough.

options.text_md: Customs EDI
options.explanation_md: Customs EDI is for trade documents.

options.text_md: The stock exchange
options.explanation_md: The stock exchange is not the reporting channel.

payload.correct_explanation_md: LRS remittances are reported through FETERS in the normal course.

payload.stem_md: A foreign bank with no presence in India wants to market in India a scheme for soliciting foreign currency deposits for its overseas branch from residents. What does it need?

options.text_md: Nothing, as it has no presence in India
options.explanation_md: Having no presence in India does not remove the requirement.

options.text_md: Prior approval of the Reserve Bank
options.explanation_md: A foreign bank soliciting foreign currency deposits from residents for its overseas branch needs prior Reserve Bank approval.

options.text_md: Only a licence from SEBI
options.explanation_md: SEBI is not the approving authority.

options.text_md: Only registration with a local magistrate
options.explanation_md: A magistrate registration is not the requirement.

payload.correct_explanation_md: A foreign bank soliciting foreign currency deposits from residents for its overseas branch needs prior Reserve Bank approval.

Reviewer for this batch is the authoring agent; no independent or human review.
